auraIntro: Welcome home, Explorer. Review the classified briefing on our home galaxy, the Milky Way.
overview: The Milky Way is a barred spiral galaxy containing our Solar System, along with an estimated 100 to 400 billion other stars.
formation: Formed approximately 13.6 billion years ago shortly after the Big Bang.
structure: Barred spiral with two major spiral arms (Scutum-Centaurus and Perseus) and a central supermassive black hole, Sagittarius A*.
discoveryHistory: Observed since antiquity as a band of light in the night sky. Democritus suggested it consisted of distant stars in 400 BCE.
observationTips: Best viewed on clear, moonless summer or autumn nights far from urban light pollution.
funFacts: Our Solar System orbits the galactic center at 828,000 km/h, taking 230 million years per cosmic orbit.
The Milky Way and Andromeda are approaching each other at 110 km/s and will merge in ~4.5 billion years.

cards.title: Galactic Overview & Home Base
cards.subtitle: Barred Spiral Architecture
cards.body: The Milky Way is our cosmic home. Spanning 100,000 light-years across, it contains an estimated 100 to 400 billion stars, interstellar gas, and dark matter.

cards.title: Formation & Cosmic Timeline
cards.subtitle: 13.6 Billion Years of Stellar Assembly
cards.body: The Milky Way began assembling ~13.6 billion years ago. Primal hydrogen gas clouds collapsed into proto-galaxies that merged over cosmic time.
bulletPoints: First generation Population III stars formed within 200 million years of the Big Bang.
Accreted smaller satellite galaxies like Gaia-Enceladus during early major mergers.
Continuous star formation maintained by gas falling in from galactic filaments.

cards.title: Spiral Morphology & Central Black Hole
cards.subtitle: Sagittarius A* and Galactic Disk Structure
cards.body: At the exact center of our galaxy lies Sagittarius A*, a supermassive black hole with a mass of 4.1 million Suns. Surrounding it is a dense bar of stars feeding two major spiral arms.
bulletPoints: Major Spiral Arms: Scutum-Centaurus Arm and Perseus Arm.
Our Sun resides in the Orion-Cygnus Spur, ~27,000 light-years from the core.
Surrounded by a halo containing over 150 ancient globular star clusters.

cards.title: Observation & Naked-Eye Astronomy
cards.subtitle: Viewing the Milky Way Band
cards.body: Galileo Galilei first resolved the hazy band of the Milky Way into individual stars using his telescope in 1610.
bulletPoints: Appears as a luminous band across the sky containing dark nebula lanes like the Great Rift.
Best observed during Summer when the bright galactic core in Sagittarius is visible.
Requires dark sky sites (Bortle Class 1-3) to see fine dust lane detail with the naked eye.

cards.title: Key Astrophysical Curiosities
cards.subtitle: Fermi Bubbles & Future Cosmic Collision
cards.body: The Milky Way is surrounded by colossal Fermi Bubbles extending 25,000 light-years above and below the galactic plane, emitting high-energy gamma rays.
bulletPoints: Fermi Bubbles were created by an energetic eruption from Sgr A* millions of years ago.
The Milky Way is currently consuming the Sagittarius Dwarf Spheroidal Galaxy.
In ~4.5 billion years, the Milky Way and Andromeda will merge into 'Milkomeda'.
